summary: No verifiable fresh signal today. Every free-source result repeated the 1 July NSW reform package already captured across the 28 June - 12 August digests: the psychological-injury 'relevant event' compensability test requiring a real and direct connection to employment with employment as the main contributing factor, the staged Whole Person Impairment thresholds (25% from 1 July 2026, rising to 27% in 2027 and 28% by 2029), the 130-week cap on weekly payments for primary psychological injury (down from up to 260 weeks), the single principal-assessment process for permanent impairment, the fixed employer excess applying to policies issued or renewed from 4pm 30 June 2026, the 1.99% Nominal Insurer premium-target freeze locked across 2026-27 and 2027-28 with Workers Compensation Industry Classification rates held flat and the minimum premium held at $240, and the section 26A enforceable psychosocial codes of practice. No new NSW regulator or tribunal release surfaced in the last 24 hours: no fresh Personal Injury Commission decision, Industrial Relations Commission determination on 'relevant conduct', SafeWork NSW prosecution or IRO release appeared. SafeWork NSW's largest-ever inspector uplift (51 additional inspectors, 20 dedicated to psychosocial risk, backed by $127.7m) and its August psychosocial inspection activity trace to the March 2026 announcement and remain documented context, not a new signal; PIC News No. 101 (10 August) falls outside today's window and carries no citable new determination; and QBE's People Risk restructure dates to October 2024. Interstate developments in range were already captured or too routine to clear the jurisdiction-weighting bar: WorkSafe Victoria holding its average premium at 1.8% for a fourth year and its WPI >20% work-capacity test, WorkCover Queensland holding its target average rate at $1.343 per $100 of wages for a second year, and ReturnToWorkSA's routine average were documented in earlier digests or are operational. No verifiable fresh AFR or SMH public headline on Australian workers compensation surfaced, so no paywalled items are captured. Sections are published empty for today.
